ClientResponses.Response:
Thank you for your feedback regarding the Q1200. We are sorry to hear your food is sticking to the grates. We are happy to help. 
 
With regards to food sticking, we have the following recommendations:
 
1. You can oil the food directly, but we do not recommend applying any kind of oil directly to the grates. 
 
2. Make sure you're giving your food enough time per side. Food will naturally start to release from the grates when close to flipping time.
 
3. If using a marinade, try to get as much excess liquid off as possible before placing the food on the grill.
 
4. If using a sauce of any kind, wait until the last 5 minutes or so to apply.
 
5. We recommend cleaning your cooking grates every time you use your grill. Simply preheat the grill on high for 15 minutes with the lid closed and then brush the grates clean with a Weber Stainless Steel Grill Brush.

Our Care team will be reaching out to follow up. Please look for our outreach soon. Thank you!

Results.ReviewText:
I purchased the Q1200 after researching reliable and high performance portable grills for RV camping. I need high enough output to give a good sear, enough area to cook a couple of courses at a time for 2-4 people, and roomy enough to fit a small Dutch oven for baking, but compact and light enough for the portability needed in my Aliner Classic.  This meets all those needs and I highly recommend it.  I purchased the optional griddle half which increases its usefulness to breakfast (eggs, hashbrowns, bacon/sausages) and grilling vegetables without having to clean dishes, a definite bonus.  

I found two drawbacks in the Q1200 regulator.  The first is that it does not turn the flame down to a low enough setting (it generally won't go below 300 degrees on the built in thermometer) reducing the ability to simmer for long times or smoke meats on the go (with a pellet tube). For this reason I give the grill 4 stars and not 5.

The second, temporary but more serious, problem (well-handled by Weber) was a failure of the regulator entirely. I have a hose to run the grill off the main propane tank and eliminate green cans (cheaper, more reliable, and more ecologically friendly). This worked extremely well all summer over 18 nights, but on a fall camp out it would not light.  After unsuccessfully trying the "regulator reset" instructions found numerous places online I was certain the regulator was faulty and needed replacement.

Weber customer service is definite plus and I was helped at the call center by a terrific agent who made me confident I was going to get the correct part which Weber shipped without cost and I got within two days.  Clear and easy replacement instructions and about 15 minutes and we are off and ready to go again. 

In short this is a terrific and convenient powerhouse of a portable grill and if the regulator tuned it down to a lower level it would be perfect.
Results.Title: Excellent grill with a pretty good regulator
